proposed_fix: Remove the platform/cache package (cache.go, cache_test.go, cache_bench_test.go, associated files), the Config.Cache field / CacheConfig type, the -cache CLI flag registration in loader.go, the two Cache.Path blocks in validation.go and EnsureDirectories, and update internal/integration/pricing_test.go to either be removed or to construct its own throwaway file cache inline if the integration test still has independent value. Confirm no other unlisted file references internal/platform/cache before deleting.
blast_radius: .env.example / docs mentioning the -cache flag or CACHE_PATH-style env var if present
acceptance_criteria: go build ./... and go test ./... (including -tags integration, after updating or removing pricing_test.go) pass with the package and config plumbing removed.
grep for 'platform/cache', 'CacheConfig', 'Cache.Path', and '-cache' flag across the repo returns no remaining references.

title: advisor.WithMaxTokens and advisor.WithTemperature functional options are never invoked; the fields they set are permanently stuck at their defaults

evidence.claim: WithMaxTokens has no call site anywhere in the tree, including its own package's tests.
evidence.output: internal/domain/advisor/service.go:41:func WithMaxTokens(n int) ServiceOption {

evidence.claim: WithTemperature has no call site anywhere in the tree, including its own package's tests.
evidence.output: internal/domain/advisor/service.go:46:func WithTemperature(t float64) ServiceOption {

evidence.claim: The only production construction of the advisor service (cmd/slabledger/init_services.go) builds its ServiceOption slice from WithLogger, WithAITracker, conditionally WithMaxToolRounds, WithScoringDataProvider, and WithGapStore — WithMaxTokens/WithTemperature are absent, so s.maxTokens and s.temperature are always left at defaultMaxTokens/defaultTemperature.
s.maxTokens and s.temperature are read only in tool_loop.go, confirming the fields are live business state — it is specifically the setter options that are unreachable, not the fields.
evidence.output: service_impl.go:55,56 (field decls), :65,66 (defaults set in constructor), tool_loop.go:49 (temp := s.temperature), tool_loop.go:55 (MaxTokens: s.maxTokens)

searched_universe: git-tracked *.go files at revision 740976ecf80a4f2ccdaa611d7790ccaa95b48773, both default and integration build tags, including _test.go files

runtime_checks.interface_satisfaction: ServiceOption is a concrete func type (func(*service)), not an interface method — no structural-typing indirection is possible here.
runtime_checks.functional_options: This IS the functional-options mechanism under direct examination: both options are defined and would compile fine if deleted, silently leaving maxTokens/temperature at their hardcoded defaults forever — matching preamble mechanism #2 exactly.
runtime_checks.serialization: Not applicable; no JSON tags on these fields.
runtime_checks.build_tags: No build tags on service.go; applies under default and integration builds alike.
runtime_checks.registration: The only DI wiring site for the advisor service (cmd/slabledger/init_services.go) does not reference either option.
runtime_checks.init_side_effects: No init() side effects construct these options.
runtime_checks.reflection_or_string: No reflection or string-keyed dispatch invokes these options.

proposed_fix: Either remove WithMaxTokens and WithTemperature (and hardcode/derive the defaults instead of exposing unreachable configurability), or wire them into cmd/slabledger/init_services.go from config if tunable max-tokens/temperature was the intent (e.g. via cfg.AdvisorRefresh, mirroring how MaxToolRounds is conditionally wired). This is a product decision, not a mechanical deletion call — flagging for the fixer to choose.
acceptance_criteria: go build ./... and go test ./... pass after either removing the two options or wiring them into cmd/slabledger/init_services.go.
If removed: git grep for WithMaxTokens and WithTemperature returns no results, and maxTokens/temperature defaults remain documented at their current values.
If wired: a config-driven override path exists and is covered by a service_test.go case analogous to the MaxToolRounds override test.

subject.identity: internal/domain/auth.Repository: GetTokens, GetTokensByUserID, UpdateTokens, DeleteTokens, DeleteAllUserTokens, CleanupExpiredOAuthStates

title: Six of auth.Repository's 24 methods are never called through the interface anywhere — five form a dead token-lifecycle path, the sixth is a separately-dead OAuth-state cleanup

evidence.claim: For each of the six candidate methods, the only occurrences anywhere in the tree are the interface declaration, the Postgres implementation, and the two test mocks — no call site through any variable of interface type auth.Repository or auth.Service exists, in production or in tests.
evidence.command: for fn in GetTokens GetTokensByUserID UpdateTokens DeleteTokens DeleteAllUserTokens CleanupExpiredOAuthStates; do git grep -n "\b$fn\b" -- '*.go'; done
evidence.output: Each of the six names resolves to exactly 4 lines: internal/domain/auth/repository.go (interface decl), internal/adapters/storage/postgres/{auth_token_store.go|auth_oauth_state_store.go} (impl), internal/testutil/mocks/auth_inmemory.go (mock), internal/testutil/mocks/auth_repository.go (mock) — zero call sites.

evidence.claim: Sanity check: the same grep technique correctly surfaces live call chains for sibling methods on the same interface (StoreTokens, GetSession, DeleteSession), which show call sites in google/oauth.go, service_impl.go, and httpserver handlers — confirming the absence of such call sites for the six candidates is a real signal, not a blind spot in the search.
evidence.command: for fn in StoreTokens GetSession DeleteSession; do git grep -n "\b$fn\b" -- '*.go' | grep -v auth_token_store.go; done
evidence.output: StoreTokens: internal/adapters/clients/google/oauth.go:307-308 (OAuthService.StoreTokens calls s.repo.StoreTokens), internal/adapters/httpserver/handlers/auth.go:208 (h.authService.StoreTokens). GetSession/DeleteSession show equivalent chains through service_impl.go and google/oauth.go.

evidence.claim: auth.Service — the interface every consumer above the repository actually holds and calls through (handlers, middleware, schedulers) — does not expose GetTokens, GetTokensByUserID, UpdateTokens, DeleteTokens, DeleteAllUserTokens, or CleanupExpiredOAuthStates at all; it only exposes StoreTokens from the token group, and CleanupExpiredSessions (a different method, for session records) instead of CleanupExpiredOAuthStates.
evidence.output: Service interface lists: GetLoginURL, ExchangeCodeForTokens, GetUserInfo, StoreOAuthState, ConsumeOAuthState, CreateSession, ValidateSession, DeleteSession, CleanupExpiredSessions, GetOrCreateUser, GetUserByID, UpdateLastLogin, StoreTokens, IsEmailAllowed, ListAllowedEmails, AddAllowedEmail, RemoveAllowedEmail, ListUsers, SetUserAdmin — the six candidates are absent.

evidence.claim: authService.s.repo (the concrete implementation backing auth.Service) never calls any of the six methods on its embedded repo field — every s.repo.X() call in service_impl.go is enumerated and none of the six appear.
evidence.output: 18 call sites listed: StoreOAuthState, ConsumeOAuthState, CreateSession, GetSession, GetUserByID, DeleteSession, DeleteExpiredSessions, GetUserByGoogleID, CreateUser, GetUserByID, UpdateUser, StoreTokens, IsEmailAllowed, ListAllowedEmails, AddAllowedEmail, RemoveAllowedEmail, ListUsers, SetUserAdmin. None of the six candidates.

evidence.claim: The only other two holders of an auth.Repository-typed variable are cmd/slabledger/main.go's authRepo (assigned then only passed into a constructor, never called directly) and google.OAuthService's embedded repo field (whose own methods — StoreTokens/GetSession/DeleteSession/etc. — were individually grepped and never call the six candidates either).
evidence.command: git grep -n 'auth\.Repository\b' -- '*.go' | grep -v '_test.go\|mocks'; git grep -n 'authRepo\.' cmd/slabledger/*.go
evidence.output: auth.Repository held by: cmd/slabledger/main.go:222 (var authRepo auth.Repository), google/oauth.go:51/62 (repo field), postgres/auth_repository.go:33 (var _ auth.Repository = ...). `authRepo.` search in cmd/slabledger produced zero method-call matches — authRepo is only assigned (main.go:231) and passed as a constructor argument (main.go:235), never has a method called on it directly.

evidence.claim: No admin/session-management handler references token revocation, per-session deletion, or OAuth-state cleanup by name, ruling out an unnamed indirect path.
evidence.output: (no output — zero matches)

searched_universe: git-tracked *.go files at revision 740976ecf80a4f2ccdaa611d7790ccaa95b48773, both default and integration build tags, including _test.go files and mock files under internal/testutil/mocks/

runtime_checks.interface_satisfaction: This is the central check for this finding, per the team lead's framing. auth.Repository is satisfied by exactly one concrete type (postgres.AuthRepository, asserted at auth_repository.go:33) plus two test mocks. The interface value itself is held in only two places (google.OAuthService.repo, cmd/slabledger's authRepo local) and neither ever calls any of the six methods through that interface value — confirmed by exhaustively grepping every call site of each method name, not by inspecting the interface declaration alone.
runtime_checks.functional_options: Not applicable; these are plain interface methods, not functional options.
runtime_checks.embedding: postgres.AuthRepository implements all six methods directly (no promotion via embedding); no other struct embeds AuthRepository or auth.Repository in a way that would promote these methods to a new, differently-named call site.
runtime_checks.serialization: None of the six methods are invoked via JSON-tag-driven (de)serialization; they are plain CRUD operations on OAuth tokens/state, not struct fields with tags.
runtime_checks.build_tags: No build tags on repository.go, auth_token_store.go, auth_oauth_state_store.go, oauth.go, or either mock file; the absence of call sites holds under both default and integration tags.
runtime_checks.registration: No scheduler builder, cmd/slabledger init file, or routes.go references any of the six method names for DI wiring or route registration.
runtime_checks.init_side_effects: No init() function constructs or calls through auth.Repository.
runtime_checks.reflection_or_string: No reflection or string-keyed dispatch invokes these methods; all six are called (in principle) via ordinary Go method syntax, which the exhaustive grep above covers.

proposed_fix: Two logically distinct removals, since the six methods split into a coherent token-lifecycle group and one unrelated method: (1) remove GetTokens, GetTokensByUserID, UpdateTokens, DeleteTokens, DeleteAllUserTokens from the auth.Repository interface, postgres.AuthRepository (auth_token_store.go), and both mocks — the per-session multi-device token read/update/delete path is entirely unused; only StoreTokens (create) is live. (2) separately remove CleanupExpiredOAuthStates from the interface, implementation (auth_oauth_state_store.go), and both mocks, or wire it into the existing session-cleanup scheduler (internal/adapters/scheduler/session_cleanup.go) if unbounded growth of the oauth_states table is an operational concern — that scheduler currently only calls CleanupExpiredSessions, not this method. Keep the auth.Repository interface itself; only these six methods and their implementations are in scope.
acceptance_criteria: go build ./... and go test ./... pass with the six methods removed from the interface, the Postgres implementation, and both mocks (or, for CleanupExpiredOAuthStates, with it wired into session_cleanup.go and covered by a scheduler test).
git grep for each of the six method names returns no results (or, for whichever is wired instead of removed, shows exactly one new call site in the scheduler plus its test).

The underlying Postgres tables/queries these methods issued are reviewed separately by the db lens before any migration is considered — this finding covers only the Go-level dead methods, not schema changes.
